videos.script: Lesson 11 started a thread per job and paid for every one. This lesson stops creating threads and starts submitting work. {{pool}} An executor keeps a few threads and hands them tasks. Ten tasks, four threads, and the same four names come back again and again. {{future}} Each task you submit gives you a Future, a receipt you exchange for the result. And when the task throws, the exception waits in the Future instead of vanishing. {{size}} How many threads should a pool have? It depends on whether the work computes or waits, and on what happens when the queue in front of the pool fills up. {{cf}} Last, CompletableFuture: ask two slow services at once, combine their answers when both arrive, and pay for the slower one instead of both.
